editorial:
Imagine waking up after years of being a mindless zombie only to find out the world has moved on without you. That is exactly where you start with this story. You follow a group of people who were cured from a cannibal virus and are now trying to fit back into a society that hates and fears them. The vibe is heavy and stressful, making you feel the struggle of these survivors as they try to remember who they were before the madness. It is not your typical zombie flick because it focuses more on the sadness and anger of the recovery process than just gore and jumping out from corners.

What really hits home is the acting, as you can feel the pain and confusion of the characters. While the pacing slows down in the middle, the tension builds up to a wild point. If you like stories that make you think about how people treat each other during a crisis, you will love this. It is a solid pick if you want something different from the usual monster movies.
endingExplained: At the end, you find out that the cure is not perfect. Some of the survivors are still dangerous and cannot control their hunger. The main characters realize that the government is not actually helping them but is instead using them for experiments. It all ends in a chaotic breakout where the line between the cured and the monsters disappears. You are left wondering if anyone can truly go back to being human after what they did.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves zombie stories with a deep plot.
